ready.name: Attraction Tickets Ltd t/a Attraction Tickets
ready.summary: A paid-for Google ad for an online seller of theme-park, sightseeing and excursion tickets made misleading claims about a price match promise.

ready.name: Cara Capsules Ltd t/a Home + Health
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad and website for a dishwasher tablet company misleadingly claimed that standard dishwasher tablets were harmful to humans and made comparative claims about the toxicity, health and safety of dishwasher tablets, without enough evidence to support these claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Cara Capsules Ltd t/a Home + Health not to claim that using standard dishwasher tablets was harmful to humans or make comparative claims about the toxicity or health and safety of dishwasher tablets, without adequate substantiation.

ready.name: Chart Prime Trading LLC
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for a financial education platform didn’t make clear that the value of investments could go down as well as up and misleadingly suggested that money could be made quickly with minimal risks.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Chart Prime Trading LLC to ensure their ads made clear that the value of financial investments could go down as well as up and that they did not mislead by suggesting money could be made quickly with minimal risks.

ready.name: Finelo Ltd
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for a financial education platform didn’t make clear that the value of investments could go down as well as up and misleadingly suggested money could be made quickly with minimal risks.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Finelo Ltd to ensure their ads made sufficiently clear that the value of financial investments could go down as well as up and that they did not mislead by suggesting money could be made quickly with minimal risks.

evidence.topic: Financial products and services Finelo Ltd Georgiou A, 83,

ready.name: HRY Games t/a AI Scorecast
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a data analytics app for football results was socially irresponsible and misleading by implying that people who used the service to make ‘informed’ gambling decisions would be very likely to turn a profit.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told HRY Games t/a AI Scorecast to ensure their future advertising was prepared with a sense of responsibility to consumers and society. We also told them to ensure their advertising did not misleadingly imply that consumers were very likely or certain to achieve a profit. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: JPD Retail Ltd t/a Harrison & James
ready.summary: A paid-for static YouTube ad and website for an online jewellery retailer misleadingly implied their business would close on a specific date. The ad also misleadingly described products as “free” and failed to ensure that reviews, ratings and testimonials were accurate and supported by evidence.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told JPD Retail Ltd t/a Harrison & James not to misleadingly state or imply that their business would close on a specific date, if that was not the case. We also told them not to describe products as “free” unless consumers were required to pay only the unavoidable cost of delivery.

ready.name: Proud & Free
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad and website for an online jewellery brand misleadingly implied they were going to cease trading and that products were available for a limited time. The ads also misleadingly described products as “free” and failed to trading identity and business address.

ready.name: Unicorn Brands Ltd t/a Nutrition Geeks
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a supplement brand made unauthorised health and nutrition claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear in the form complained of. We told Unicorn Brands Ltd t/a Nutrition Geeks to ensure any specific health and nutrition claims made in their future advertising were authorised on the GB NHC Register and complied with the conditions of use for those claims.

ready.name: Care Pharma Bradford Ltd t/a The Care Pharmacy
ready.summary: A paid-for Google search ad for an online pharmacy promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Care Pharmacy Bradford Ltd t/a The Care Pharmacy not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Express Healthcare Ltd t/a pharmacyonline
ready.summary: Two paid-for Meta ads and a website for an online pharmacy made medicinal claims and promoted unlicensed products. They also promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Express Healthcare Ltd t/a Pharmacy Online not to make medicinal claims for, or promote, unlicensed products, or promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Juniper Technologies UK Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Google ad for an online pharmacy promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: MedExpress Enterprises Ltd t/a MedExpress
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for MedExpress promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told MedExpress Enterprises Ltd t/a MedExpress not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Menwell Ltd t/a Do Health
ready.summary: Two ads for a health app incorporating a blood testing programme misleadingly implied that their blood tests could prevent and diagnose medical conditions or that their service could provide more tailored specific advice than pre-existing advice, without the evidence to support these claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Menwell Ltd t/a Do Health not to imply that their blood tests could prevent and diagnose medical conditions, or that their service could provide more tailored, specific advice than pre-existing generic advice if they did not hold evidence to substantiate such claims.

ready.name: Simple Online Healthcare Ltd t/a Simple Online Pharmacy
ready.summary: Two paid-for social media ads for an online pharmacy made medicinal claims and promoted unlicensed products. They also promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Simple Online Healthcare Ltd t/a Simple Online Pharmacy not to make medicinal claims for, or promote, unlicensed products, or promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Esaverwatt.com t/a StopWatt
ready.summary: A product listing on Amazon for a smart home energy monitoring brand misleadingly exaggerated the effectiveness of the product by making claims that it could save electricity, reduce electricity waste and lower energy bills.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Esaverwatt.com t/a StopWatt not to mislead consumers by exaggerating the effectiveness of the product. Specifically, we told StopWatt not to repeat claims that the product could save electricity, reduce electricity waste or lower energy bills. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Huel Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram video and pre-roll ad on YouTube for Huel was irresponsible by encouraging the exclusive consumption of Huel in place of conventional food. The ads also made unathorised specific health claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Huel Ltd to ensure that future marketing communications did not encourage or condone the exclusive consumption of Huel in place of conventional food.

ready.name: Luma Pet
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for Luma Pet misleadingly claimed that a red light therapy pad could reduce inflammation around the spinal discs, treat existing spinal damages or back pain and prevent IVDD related flare ups without having the evidence to support these claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Luma Pet Ltd not to claim that its red-light therapy pad could reduce inflammation around the spinal discs, treat existing spinal damage or back pain, prevent IVDD-related flare-ups or paralysis, unless they held adequate evidence to substantiate the claims. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: International Medical Center LLC t/a Swiss Medica
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for a medical clinic made misleading claims that stem cell treatment could treat or alleviate the traits associated with autism.
ready.action: The ad must not appear in the form investigated. We told International Medical Center LLC t/a Swiss Media XXI Century not to state or imply that their stem cell treatment could treat or alleviate the traits of autism unless they held robust evidence to substantiate the claim. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Linden Clinics t/a Linden Stem Cell
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a stem cell therapy clinic made misleading claims that stem cell therapy was effective in improving the traits associated with autism in children.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Linden Clinics t/a Linden Stem Cell not to make claims that stem cell therapy was effective in improving the traits associated with autism in children, unless they held robust evidence to substantiate those claims.

ready.name: Morley's (Fast Foods) Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram post by Ellie Scotney for Morley’s UK broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Morley’s (Fast Foods) Ltd t/a Morley’s to ensure that their paid-for ads on the internet were not for identifiable “less healthy” foods.

ready.name: Reliable Medicare Ltd

ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Reliable Medicare Ltd to ensure their savings claims did not misleadingly imply savings against the usual selling price of a product.

ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Rumi Pulse t/a Rumi Pulse Medical Tourism Agency not to state or imply that their stem cell treatment could treat or alleviate the traits of autism unless they held robust evidence to substantiate the claim.

ready.name: Whitworths Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram post on the WhitworthsUK page made unauthorised health claims and implied that a food could prevent or treat human disease.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Whitworths Limited not to make health claims for foods unless they were authorised on the applicable register, or had the same meaning for consumers as an authorised claim.

ready.name: McCain Foods (GB) Ltd t/a McCain Foodservice Solutions
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for McCain Foods and Five Akhi’s restaurants broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told McCain Foods (GB) Ltd t/a McCain Foodservice Solutions to ensure their paid-for ads on the internet were not for an identifiable “less healthy” food.

ready.name: Hemios
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad and a paid-for YouTube display ad for a magnetic bracelet made misleading claims in relation to weight-loss and improving erectile performance.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Hemios not to make efficacy claims about their product, for example in relation to weight loss, or improving erectile performance, in the absence of adequate evidence.

ready.name: Lotus Leisure Ltd t/a DialAFlight
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for a travel agent didn’t make the basis for their environmental claims clear.
ready.action: The ad must remain withdrawn. We told Lotus International Ltd t/a DialAFlight to ensure they made the basis of any environmental claims clear.

ready.name: OneStream Ltd
ready.summary: A website for OneStream didn’t make clear that their broadband packages included free trials that automatically renewed for a fee.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Onestream Ltd to ensure their ads made sufficiently clear that their broadband packages included free trials that would automatically renew for a fee.

ready.name: Thomas Cook Tourism (UK) Company Ltd t/a Thomas Cook
ready.summary: A paid- for Google ad for Thomas Cook didn’t make the basis for their environmental claims clear.
ready.action: The ad must remain amended or withdrawn. We told Thomas Cook Tourism (UK) Company Ltd t/a Thomas Cook to ensure they made the basis of any environmental claims clear.

evidence.topic: Holidays, travel and motoring Thomas Cook Tourism (UK)

ready.name: We Love Holidays Ltd t/a loveholidays
ready.summary: Two paid-for Google ads for loveholidays didn’t make the basis for their environmental claims clear.
ready.action: The ads must be amended or withdrawn. We told We Love Holidays Ltd t/a loveholidays to ensure they made the basis of any environmental claims clear.

ready.name: ATR Brands Ltd t/a Antler
ready.summary: Two emails and a website page for a luggage retailer misleadingly implied a promotion included all products they sold, by stating a promotion related to “everything” or applied “sitewide” when this was not the case.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told ATR Brands Ltd t/a Antler to ensure their ads did not state or imply that a promotion included all products they sold, including by stating that a promotion related to “everything” or applied “sitewide”, if that was not the case.

ready.name: Frasers Group Trading Ltd t/a Sports Direct
ready.summary: A product page on the Sports Direct website made misleading claims about reference price and associated savings.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Frasers Group Trading Ltd t/a Sports Direct to ensure that future price comparisons did not mislead by falsely claiming a price advantage, and that references to RRPs reflected the price at which the product concerned was generally sold across the market.

ready.name: Glow Up LLC t/a Maxxing
ready.summary: Two paid-for Meta ads for an AI powered app to maximise physical attractiveness misleadingly exaggerated the effectiveness of the product, were irresponsible and included gender stereotypes that were likely to cause harm.

ready.name: Kind Patches Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for a supplement company, misleadingly implied their products had health benefits without supporting evidence and irresponsibly trivialised and condoned an act of anti-social behaviour.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Kind Patches Ltd not to state or imply that their products had health benefits without holding adequate substantiation for such claims. We also told them to ensure their ads were prepared responsibly and did not condone anti-social behaviour.

ready.name: SheMed Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Reddit ad for a female-focused medical weight-loss service promoted weight-loss prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules, was likely to exploit consumers’ insecurities relating to body image and weight and was irresponsible.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told SheMed Ltd t/a SheMed not to promote POMs to the public in future and to ensure any ads for non-POMs conformed with the Summary of Product Characteristics in the relevant marketing authorisation. We also told them to ensure their future advertising was prepared with a sense of responsibility to consumers and society.

ready.name: BioIdentical Hormone Therapy Ltd t/a BioID Health
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for a hormone health consultant made misleading claims that they could provide more effective tests and services for low testosterone than GPs and were irresponsible by implying that GPs were insufficiently thorough.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We reminded BioIdentical Hormone Therapy Ltd t/a BioID Health not to make claims regarding the effectiveness of their tests and services unless they held robust evidence to substantiate them, and not to imply that GPs were insufficiently thorough.

ready.name: Hotpoint UK Appliances Ltd
ready.summary: A website for Hotpoint made misleading comparative claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Hotpoint UK Appliances Ltd to ensure future comparative claims did not mislead by omitting information about the nature of the comparison.

ready.name: Nutri-Paw Ltd t/a Healthy Dog
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a dog dental care product misleadingly and irresponsibly implied that dogs undergoing veterinary treatment had a high chance of dying, made medicinal claims for an unauthorised product, and made misleading efficacy claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told NutriPaw Ltd t/a Healthy Dog to not make efficacy claims unless they held adequate, robust evidence and not to make medicinal claims for an unauthorised product. We also told them not to misleadingly and irresponsibly imply dogs undergoing veterinary treatment had a higher chance of dying.

ready.name: Vir Health Ltd t/a Numan
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for a digital healthcare company made misleading claims about the occurrence of low testosterone in the male population.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Vir Health Ltd t/a Numan not to make claims about the occurrence of low testosterone in the male population without adequate substantiation.

ready.name: Fenix Biomed BV
ready.summary: A website for a human tissue donation service misleadingly implied they were based in the UK.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Fenix Biomed BV t/a A Love of Humanity not to imply they was based in the UK when that was not the case.

ready.name: The Boots Company PLC t/a Boots
ready.summary: A national press ad for Boots featured a promotion that wasn’t administered fairly and caused participants unnecessary disappointment.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again the form complained of. We told The Boots Company PLC t/a Boots and Associated Newspapers Ltd t/a The Mail on Sunday to ensure that their promotions were administered fairly and that they did not cause participants unnecessary disappointment.

ready.name: Gary Baron
ready.summary: A webpage for Gary Baron Counselling claimed that he was a member of the British Association of Counsellors and Psycotherapists when this wasn’t the case.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Gary Baron not to claim in future that he was BACP accredited if that was not the case. We referred the matter to CAP's Compliance team.

ready.name: Nectar Sleep Ltd
ready.summary: The homepage for the Nectar Sleep website made misleading saving claims and didn’t make the basis of their savings claims clear. They also made comparisons against other brands’ prices without ensuring the claims were based on the actual price of the product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Nectar Sleep Ltd to ensure that future “save up to” claims were not misleading and that they made the basis of their savings claims clear. We also told them to ensure that comparisons against other brands’ prices were based on actual prices for those products.

ready.name: YO! Sushi UK Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram post for YO! Sushi broke the rules by featuring an identifiable specific less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told YO! Sushi UK Ltd t/a YO! to ensure their paid ads on the internet were not for identifiable less healthy foods, such as through the inclusion of text that depicted a specific less healthy food product.

ready.name: Costcutter Supermarkets Group Ltd t/a Costcutter and Mondelez Europe Services GmbH – UK branch t/a Cadbury (Mondelez)
ready.summary: A webpage for Costcutter and Cadburys broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product. Another ad was investigated but it didn’t break our rules.

ready.name: Innate-Essence Ltd t/a the Turmeric Co.
ready.summary: A website for a turmeric shot company made claims that a food could prevent, treat or cure human disease.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Innate-Essence Ltd t/a the Turmeric Co. to ensure their future advertising did not make claims that food could prevent, treat or cure human disease.

ready.name: Airbrush
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads and a website for a hairstyling company misleadingly implied they were endorsed by fashion brands, used unrelated influencer content to promote their product and didn’t have evidence to show that testimonials were genuine.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the forms complained of. We told Airbrush UK to ensure their ads did not misleadingly imply they were endorsed by fashion brands. We also told them not to misleadingly use content relating to competitor products to promote their product. We also told them to ensure they held substantiation to show that any testimonials used were genuine.

ready.name: Bolt Healthcare Ltd t/a Bolt Pharmacy
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for an online pharmacy failed to make their commercial intent clear and falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their trade by presenting websites used for advertising purposes as independent review sites.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Bolt Healthcare Ltd t/a Bolt Pharmacy operating UK Weight Loss Reviews to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example, by presenting accounts used for marketing purposes as independent review sites in paid-for ads.

ready.name: Bolt Healthcare Ltd t/a Bolt Pharmacy
ready.summary: Two paid-for Facebook ads for an online pharmacy promoted weight loss prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Bolt Healthcare Ltd t/a Bolt Pharmacy not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Utility Warehouse Ltd
ready.summary: A page on a mobile phone operator’s website didn’t make sure that their unlimited claims were directly qualified with the terms of their fair use policy. Another issue was investigated but it didn’t break our rules.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Utility Warehouse Ltd t/a Utility Warehouse to ensure that their unlimited claims were directly qualified with the terms of their fair use policy.

ready.name: Domino's Pizza UK & Ireland Ltd t/a Domino's
ready.media: Social media (paid ad), Television, Video on demand
ready.summary: A TV ad, Video on Demand ad and a YouTube ad for Domino’s broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.

ready.name: Higham Miller Coffee Ltd t/a Exhale Healthy Coffee
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for a coffee company made unauthorised health and nutrition claims and included health claims that referred to the recommendation of an individual health professional.
ready.action: The ad must not appear in the form complained of. We told Higham Miller Coffee Ltd t/a Exhale Coffee to ensure any specific health and nutrition claims made in their future advertising were authorised on the GB NHC Register and complied with the conditions of use for those claims. Additionally, any general health claims needed to be accompanied by a relevant authorised specific health claim.

ready.name: Eurowings GmbH t/a Eurowings
ready.summary: A paid-for Google ad for an airline gave a misleading impression of their flights environmental impact and implied that people could pay to fully offset the carbon emissions from a specific flight without suitable evidence to support these claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Eurowings GmbH to ensure future ads did not give a misleading impression of the impact caused by travelling with them, and that they did not state or imply consumers could pay to fully offset the carbon emissions from a specific flight unless they held suitably robust substantiation to support the claims.

ready.name: Kind Patches Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a supplement company made claims that a supplement patch could help with weight-loss and made medicinal claims for products that weren’t authorised by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA).
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Kind Patches Ltd not to make medicinal claims for products that did not have the necessary authorisation. We also told them to ensure their ads were prepared with a sense of responsibility to consumers and to society, and did not include harmful gender stereotypes that were likely to cause harm, or serious or widespread offence.

ready.name: Origin Sleep UK Ltd t/a Origin Mattress
ready.summary: A website for a mattress company made misleading savings claims and misleadingly implied that discount offers were time-limited and that people needed to act more quickly than necessary to take advantage of an offer.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Origin Sleep UK Ltd to ensure that pricing claims should not suggest a saving against a product when it was actually referring to a saving based on an additional free item.

ready.name: Parker Products Ltd t/a ParkerBrand
ready.summary: A website ad for a pressure washer made misleading savings claims and stated savings against previous prices without evidence that the product was normally sold at that price.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Parker Products Ltd t/a ParkerBrand to ensure their future savings claims did not mislead and were substantiated against the usual selling price of their products. We told them not to state savings against previous prices unless it could be evidenced that the product was generally sold at that price.

ready.name: Phlo Technologies Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad promoted weight-loss prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Phlo Technologies Ltd t/a Morrisons Clinic and Wm Morrison Supermarkets Ltd t/a Morrisons not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Qatar Airways Group QCSC t/a Qatar Airways
ready.summary: Two paid-for LinkedIn posts for an airline gave a misleading impression of their flights environmental impact and implied that people could pay to fully offset the carbon emissions of a specific flight without suitable evidence to support this claim.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated.

ready.name: Capgroup Inc Ltd
ready.summary: A website for a whiskey cask and gold coin investment company made misleading claims about investment returns. As well as misleadingly presenting an incorrect Trustpilot score.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Capgroup Int Ltd to ensure that their ads did not mislead by presenting an incorrect Trustpilot score or imply that news publications had chosen to run editorial features on them, if that was not the case.

ready.name: Mars Wrigley Confectionery UK Ltd t/a Mars
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for M&M’s broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product through the inclusion of a character that depicted a specific less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again the form complained of. We told Mars Wrigley Confectionery UK Ltd t/a Mars to ensure their paid-for ads on the internet were not for identifiable “less healthy” foods, such as through the inclusion of a character that depicted a specific “less healthy” food product.

ready.name: S&E1 Ltd t/a Morley's Woking
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for Morley’s broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told S&E1 Ltd t/a Morley’s Woking to ensure that their paid-for ads on the internet were not for identifiable “less healthy” foods.

ready.name: Stove Industry Alliance Ltd t/a Stove Industry Association (SIA)
ready.summary: [Republished ruling] A website for the Stove Industry Association made unsubstantiated claims that modern stoves emitted significantly lower emissions than open fireplaces or older stoves, and that they were a low-emission way to heat a home. It also failed to make the basis of comparative environmental claims clear.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Stove Industry Alliance Ltd t/a Stove Industry Association to ensure that all objective claims were adequately substantiated in future ads and that appropriate qualification was used to explain the limitations of claims where relevant. We reminded them that the basis of comparative environmental claims must be made clear.

ready.name: Cablelinker Electronics Ltd t/a Aquoxis
ready.summary: A YouTube pre-roll ad and two online display ads for a pressure washer misleadingly exaggerated the functionality of the product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Cablelinker Electronics Ltd t/a Aquoxis to ensure their ads did not misleadingly exaggerate the functionality of their products in the future, for example, by stating or implying that their product’s performance exceeded that of traditional pressure washers if that was not the case. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: YN Netcom Ltd t/a BeeHome
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a cordless pressure washer misleadingly exaggerated the functionality of the product and claimed they had a high rating based on customer reviews when this was not the case.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told YN Netcom Ltd t/a BeeHomie to ensure their ads did not misleadingly exaggerate the functionality of their products in the future, for example, by stating or implying that their product’s performance was comparable to that of a traditional pressure washer if that was not the case.

ready.name: Adidas UK Ltd t/a adidas
ready.summary: A paid-for Google ad for adidas made misleading environmental claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Adidas UK Ltd t/a adidas to ensure that their future ads made the basis of any environmental claims clear and did not suggest their running shoes or other products were entirely made from recycled materials when that was not the case, and that a high level of substantiation must be held to support absolute claims.

ready.name: Argos Limited t/a Argos
ready.summary: A page in the Argos 2025 Christmas gift guide featuring the video game Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 failed to make clear that the game contained loot boxes. Another ad was investigated but it didn’t break the rules.

ready.name: Big Fang Collective Ltd t/a Golf Fang
ready.summary: A leaflet for an indoor golf venue didn’t make clear it was an ad and caused unjustified distress by resembling a parking ticket.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Big Fang Collective t/a Golf Fang to ensure that all future marketing communications were obviously identifiable as such and made clear their financial intent. We also told them to ensure their future ads did not cause unjustified distress to consumers, for example by resembling parking tickets.

ready.name: Calvin Klein Europe BV t/a Calvin Klein
ready.summary: A paid-for Google ad for Calvin Klein made misleading environmental claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Calvin Klein Europe B.V. t/a Calvin Klein to ensure that their future ads made the basis of any environmental claims clear and did not suggest that their products were made entirely from recycled, organic or other environmentally preferred materials when that was not the case.

ready.name: Express Healthcare Ltd t/a pharmacyonline.co.uk
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad and website for an online pharmacy promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told Express Healthcare Ltd t/a pharmacyonline.co.uk not to promote POMs to the public in future. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Microsoft Ltd t/a Microsoft
ready.summary: Two digital posters for the Xbox Game Pass failed to make clear that the games shown in the posters included in game purchases.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Microsoft Ltd to ensure that ads for the Xbox Game Pass, which featured identifiable video games, disclosed the presence of in-game purchases.

ready.name: Motorpoint Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for a used car retailer made misleading savings claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Motorpoint to ensure that their future savings claims did not mislead and that, when making “up to £x off” claims, they should ensure that a significant proportion of vehicles were available with savings of the stated amount and that such claims represented the true overall picture.

ready.name: Parc AI Ltd t/a Parc
ready.summary: A leaflet for a car parking app didn’t make clear it was an ad and caused unjustified distress by resembling a parking ticket.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Parc AI Ltd t/a Parc to ensure that all future marketing communications were obviously identifiable as such and made clear their commercial intent. We also told them to ensure their future ads did not cause unjustified distress to consumers, for example, by resembling parking tickets.

ready.name: The Clean Supps LLC t/a Inno Supps
ready.summary: Four paid-for Meta ads promoting supplements made claims that a food supplement could prevent, treat or cure human diseases or conditions, made unauthorised health claims and made claims that referred to a rate or amount of weight loss for food supplements.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told The Clean Supps LLC t/a Inno Supps not to claim that a food supplement could prevent, treat or cure human disease, or make medicinal claims for a product that did not have the necessary authorisation; not to make health claims for food supplements unless those claims were authorised on the GB Register and met the conditions of use.

ready.name: Uniqlo (UK) Ltd t/a UNIQLO
ready.summary: A paid- for Google ad for UNIQLO made misleading environmental claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told UNIQLO Europe Ltd t/a UNIQLO to ensure that their future ads made the basis of any environmental claims clear and did not suggest that their products were entirely made from recycled materials when that was not the case, and that a high level of substantiation must be held to support absolute claims.

ready.name: BetterYou Ltd t/a Better You
ready.summary: A magazine ad for a supplement company made misleading claims that their product delivered vitamin D “quickly” and enabled fast absorption of vitamin D into the body.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told BetterYou Ltd not to make claims that their product delivered vitamin D “quickly” or claims that implied their product enabled fast absorption of vitamin D into the body, unless they held sufficient robust evidence to substantiate those claims.

ready.name: HealthTracker Apps t/a Blood Pressure Monitor App
ready.summary: Two paid-for in-app ads for a health app made medical claims for a product that wasn’t registered as a medical device and misleadingly implied that their app could monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told HealthTracker Apps t/a Blood Pressure Monitor App not to make medical claims for devices that did not hold the applicable conformity marking and were not registered with the MHRA.

ready.name: Hume Health LLC t/a HumeHealth
ready.summary: Three paid-for YouTube ads and a paid-for Facebook ad for Hume Health made medical claims for products that weren’t registered as medical devices, discouraged essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought and exaggerated the capabilities of their products.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Hume Health LLC not to make medical claims for devices that did not hold the applicable conformity marking and were not registered with the MHRA. We also told them not to exaggerate the capabilities of their products. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: MN2S Management Ltd t/a MN2S
ready.summary: A website for a talent agency misleadingly stated that Seph Lawless was represented by the agency and was available to be booked through them.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told MN2S Management Ltd t/a MN2S to ensure that it did not misleadingly state or imply that a person was represented by their agency and was available to be booked through them, if that was not the case. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Novabeyond Ltd t/a Blood Pressure-Monitor Tracker App
ready.summary: An in-app ad and a paid-for Google ad for a health app made medical claims for a product that wasn’t registered as a medical device and made misleading claims that their product could monitor blood pressure.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Novabeyond Ltd t/a Blood Pressure-Tracker Monitor App not to make medical claims for devices that did not hold the applicable conformity marking and were not registered with the MHRA. We also told them not to state or imply that their product could monitor blood pressure unless they held adequate evidence to support their claims.

ready.name: P&L Studio t/a Blood Pressure
ready.summary: A paid-for in-app ad for a health app misleadingly implied that it could monitor blood pressure and heart rate.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told P&L Studio t/a Blood Pressure not to state or imply that their product could monitor blood pressure or heart rate, including through its product name, unless they held adequate evidence for such claims. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team

ready.name: Pure Cremation Funeral Planning Ltd t/a Pure Cremation
ready.summary: A TV ad for Pure Cremation misleadingly implied that their standard funeral plan included an attended funeral service and failed to make clear where a plan was limited to a non-attended cremation.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Pure Cremation Funeral Planning Ltd t/a Pure Cremation to ensure their ads did not imply that their standard funeral plan included an attended funeral service if it did not, and to make clear where a plan was limited to a non-attended cremation.

ready.name: StudySmarter GmbH
ready.summary: Three job listings on a student resource website misleadingly implied they were genuine job vacancies and falsely implied that the advertiser was acting for purposes outside its business.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told StudySmarter GmbH to ensure that its ads did not mislead by implying they related to genuine vacancies if that was not the case.

ready.name: This is Enough Ltd
ready.summary: [Republished ruling] A website, LinkedIn post and GoFundMe page promoting DNA testing kits for victims of sexual assault made misleading claims about the incidence of rapes and the potential for evidence gathered using their self-testing kit to be admissible in court.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current forms. We told This is Enough Ltd t/a Enough not to state or imply that evidence gathered using their self-testing kit was admissible in court unless they held adequate substantiation for those claims.

ready.name: Amazon Europe Core Sarl t/a Amazon.co.uk
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for Amazon Fresh UK broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Amazon Europe Core Sarl (t/a Amazon Fresh) to ensure their paid ads on the internet were not for identifiable less healthy foods.

ready.name: Beauty Pie Ltd t/a Beauty Pie Ltd
ready.summary: A poster for an LED face mask made misleading claims that it was clinically proven to reduce wrinkles in 4 weeks.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Beauty Pie Ltd not to state the C-Wave Facial LED treatment mask was “clinically proven to reduce wrinkles in 4 weeks” unless they held adequate substantiation to support the claim.

ready.name: Fortore Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for an investment competition website failed to make clear that gold and precious metal investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Fortore Ltd to ensure that future marketing made clear that gold and precious metal investment was unregulated. We further told them, to make clear that the value of investments was variable and could go down as well as up.

ready.name: Montford Group Ltd t/a Brittania Bullion
ready.summary: A paid-for LinkedIn ad for a gold investment company failed to make clear that physical gold investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Montford Group Ltd t/a Britannia Bullion to ensure that future marketing made clear that physical gold investment was unregulated. We further told them to make clear that the value of investments was variable and could go down as well as up.

ready.name: RE/MAX Property Specialists t/a Billie Dunlop
ready.summary: A leaflet and a Facebook post for an estate agency service made misleading and unverifiable comparisons with identifiable competitors.

ready.name: Rosland Capital Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a gold and precious metal specialist failed to make clear that gold and precious metal investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Rosland Capital t/a Rosland Gold to ensure that future marketing made clear that gold and precious metal investment was unregulated. We told them to make clear that the value of investments was variable and could go down as well as up and that examples of past performance or experience were not necessarily a guide to the future.

ready.name: Sourced Consultancy Ltd t/a Oak & Mason
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for a gold investment company failed to make clear that physical gold investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable. The ad also broke the rules by referencing an example of past performance that was unrepresentative.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Sourced Consultancy Ltd t/a Oak and Mason to ensure that future marketing made clear that physical gold investment was unregulated. We told them to make clear that the value of investments was variable and could go down as well as up and that examples of past performance or experience were not necessarily a guide to the future.

ready.name: Tarvos Ltd t/a 7879
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for an online retailer of gold and platinum jewellery failed to make clear that physical gold and precious metal investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Tarvos Ltd t/a 7879.co to ensure that future marketing made clear that physical gold and precious metal investment was unregulated. We further told them to make clear that the value of investments was variable and could go down as well as up.

ready.name: Brighton & Hove City Council
ready.summary: A digital poster misleadingly implied there was a direct causal link between the use of wood burners and open fires and an increase in particle pollution, without having suitable evidence to back this claim up.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Brighton & Hove City Council to ensure that robust evidence was held to substantiate any claims where a direct causal link between the use of wood burners and open fires and an increase in particle pollution was stated or implied.

ready.name: Wowcher Ltd t/a Wowcher
ready.summary: A promotion on the Wowcher website wasn’t administered fairly and caused unnecessary disappointment.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Wowcher Ltd and PCM Travels UK Ltd t/a The Travel Makers to ensure that their promotions were administered fairly and to ensure that their promotions did not cause unnecessary disappointment. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Guangzhoushi Yingyi Maoyi Youxiangongsi t/a LANPN
ready.summary: An Instagram post on Gemma Markland’s account wasn’t obviously identifiable as an ad.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Guangzhoushi Yingyi Maoyi Youxiangongsi t/a LANPN and Gemma Markland to ensure that their future ads were obviously identifiable as marketing communications, that the commercial intent was made clear, and that identifiers such as “ad” were clearly and prominently displayed.

ready.name: Menwell Ltd t/a Voy
ready.summary: Three emails for an online pharmacy promoted prescription-only medicines to the public against the law and our rules. The ads were also socially irresponsible by creating an undue sense of urgency for people who were considering medicated weight-loss programmes.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Menwell Ltd t/a Voy not to promote POMs to the public in future and to ensure their future advertising did not create an undue sense of urgency for consumers considering medicated weight loss programmes.

ready.name: Boots UK Ltd t/a boots.com
ready.summary: An online display ad for Boots made misleading savings claims. Another ad was investigated but it didn’t break the rules.

ready.name: DBZ Marketplace Online Ltd t/a Debenhams
ready.summary: Two video display banners for Debenhams made misleading savings claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told DBZ Marketplace Online Ltd t/a Debenhams to ensure that their future savings claims did not mislead and were substantiated against the usual selling price of the products.

ready.name: SnackVerse Ltd
ready.summary: A webpage for a snack subscription box misleadingly implied their subscribers would receive a specific country-themed box but didn’t make clear this was subject to allocation conditions.
ready.action: The ad must not appear in its current form. We told SnackVerse Ltd to ensure their ads did not imply their subscribers had received a specific country-themed box for a given month if that was subject to allocation conditions.

ready.name: 111 Skin Ltd t/a 111skin
ready.summary: A product listing for a skincare product misleadingly exaggerated the effects of a cosmetic product for ageing skin.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told 111SKIN Ltd to not misleadingly exaggerate the effects of cosmetic products on the signs of ageing in facial skin.

ready.name: Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board t/a AHDB
ready.media: National newspaper (paid ad), Website (own site), Television, Social media (own site)
ready.summary: Two national press ads made claims about the carbon footprints of beef and milk that weren’t supported with full life cycle evidence. Two other issues were investigated in relation to TV ads, an Instagram post, and a website page but they didn’t break the rules.

ready.name: Course Accreditation Ltd
ready.summary: A website and a paid-for Google search ad for an accreditation company didn’t provide suitable evidence to back up objective claims, including comparative claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Course Accreditation Ltd to ensure they held documentary evidence to substantiate any objective claims, including those regarding the experience of their assessors, their global recognition, any claim to be a “UK-leading body”, and any other comparative claims.

ready.name: Linjer Ltd
ready.summary: Two paid-for Google ads for a jewellery retailer didn’t make clear that their diamonds were synthetic.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Linjer Ltd not to misleadingly use the term “diamond” to describe their synthetic diamonds in isolation without a clear and prominent qualifier, such as “synthetic” or wording of the same meaning.

ready.name: Novita Diamonds Ltd t/a Novita Diamonds
ready.summary: Two paid-for Meta ads for a jewellery retailer didn’t make clear that their diamonds were synthetic.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Novita Diamonds Ltd not to misleadingly use the term “diamond” to describe their synthetic diamonds in isolation without a clear and prominent qualifier, such as “synthetic” or wording of the same meaning.

ready.name: GLP-1 Pro Ltd t/a GuLP-1
ready.summary: Two webpages for a food supplement company made claims that a supplement could prevent, treat or cure human disease and made unauthorised health and medicinal claims.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told GLP-1 Pro Ltd t/a Gulp not to make specific health claims unless they were authorised on the GB NHC Register, including through product names. We told them not to claim that a food supplement could prevent, treat or cure human disease, or make medicinal claims for a product that did not have the necessary authorisation.

ready.name: Medilife Clinic Enfield
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for a health clinic made claims that their treatments could alleviate or treat the traits of autism without suitable evidence to support these claims. The ad also discouraged essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Medilife Clinic Enfield not to state or imply that QEEG and TMS could treat or alleviate the traits of autism unless they held robust evidence to substantiate the claim. We also told them to ensure their future ads did not discourage essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought.

ready.name: The Professional Development Consortium Ltd t/a CPD Standards Office
ready.summary: Two paid-for Meta ads for a training accreditation company made misleading comparative claims with identifiable competitors which weren’t supported by evidence and couldn’t be verified by consumers.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told The Professional Development Consortium Ltd t/a CPD Standards Office to ensure that future comparative claims made with identifiable competitors were not misleading, were supported by adequate documentary evidence and could be verified by consumers.

ready.name: Bakkavor Ltd
ready.summary: A promotion featured on the packaging of a cookie dough dessert misleadingly implied that particular products were included in the promotion, causing unnecessary disappointment.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Bakkavor Foods Ltd t/a The Pizza Company not to imply that particular products were included in future promotions if that was not the case, and to ensure that they administered their future promotions fairly and avoided causing unnecessary disappointment.

ready.name: Beiersdorf UK Ltd
ready.summary: A poster ad for Eucerin Skincare misleadingly claimed that a serum was clinically proven to make you look up to 5 years younger.
ready.action: The ad should not appear again in the form complained of. We told Beiersdorf UK Ltd t/a Eucerin not to state or imply that you could “look up to 5 years younger” with Eucerin Hyaluron-Filler Epigenetic Serum product, unless they held robust evidence to substantiate the claim.

ready.name: CC Response NW Ltd
ready.summary: Two paid-for Google search listings and a web landing page for an accident claims management company failed to make the nature of their service clear, misleadingly implied there was no cost to consumers and made misleading claims in relation to potential savings.

evidence.topic: Holidays, travel and motoring CC Response NW Ltd C/O

ready.name: Exclusive Law Ltd
ready.summary: Three paid-for Google search listings and a website for an accident claims management company failed to make the nature of their service clear, misleadingly implied there was no cost to consumers and irresponsibly discouraged consumers from approaching their insurance provider.

ready.name: Gismart Ltd t/a Dancebit
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a dance workout app misleadingly stated that their service was free.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Gismart Ltd t/a Dancebit to ensure that it did not unconditionally state or imply their service was “free” if consumers had to pay upfront and could only obtain reimbursement subsequently and subject to conditions.

ready.name: iRevolution Claims Ltd
ready.summary: Three Google search listings and a website for an accident claims management company failed to make the nature of their service clear and misleadingly implied there was no cost to consumers.

ready.name: Birling Shore Ltd t/a ShroomIQ
ready.summary: A website and paid-for Facebook ad for a children’s supplement brand stated that a food supplement could prevent, treat or cure the symptoms of ADHD, Tourette Syndrome, anxiety and depression.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Birling Shore Ltd t/a ShroomIQ not to state or imply that their food supplements could prevent, treat or cure human disease, which included claims to treat or cure the symptoms of ADHD, Tourette Syndrome, anxiety and depression. We also told them not to make medicinal claims for products that were not authorised by the MHRA.

ready.name: Dollead Technology Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for search ad for a vacuum review website failed to make their commercial intent clear and falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their trade by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Dollead Technology Ltd t/a trustedguide.org to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example, by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites in paid-for ads. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Easy as HGV Ltd
ready.summary: Three websites for Heavy Goods Vehicle (HGV) training service providers made misleading claims about HGV test pass rates and falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their business.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Easy as HGV Ltd to ensure that pass rate claims were not misleading and could be substantiated. We also told them to ensure that they did not falsely imply they were acting for purposes outside their business.

ready.name: Ecoflow Innovation UK
ready.summary: A website for a sustainable energy company misleadingly claimed that their products could be installed without using a certified installer or electrician.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again the form complained of. We told Ecoflow Innovation UK t/a EcoFlow to ensure that their future ads did not misleadingly state or imply that their products could be installed without using a certified installer or electrician if that was not the case.

ready.name: Global Health Tests Ltd t/a Check My Body Health
ready.summary: A website for a Bioresonance hair test misleadingly claimed that the test could comprehensively analyse body intolerances.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Global Health Tests Ltd t/a Check My Body Health not to state or imply that their Bioresonance hair test could comprehensively analyse body intolerances without holding adequate substantiation.

ready.name: HGV Learning
ready.summary: A website for a Heavy Goods Vehicle (HGV) training service provider made misleading claims about HGV test pass rates.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told HGV Learning to ensure that pass rate claims were not misleading and that all such claims could be substantiated.

ready.name: HGVT Ltd
ready.summary: A website and pages for Heavy Goods Vehicle (HGV) training service providers made misleading claims about HGV test pass rates, the nature of a promotion and being the largest and best rated HGV training provider. The ad also falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their business.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told HGVT Ltd not to make “up to” claims unless a significant proportion of items were available at the advertised maximum discount, to ensure that seasonal offers and pass rate claims were not misleading, and that all such claims could be substantiated.

ready.name: L'Oréal (UK) Ltd
ready.summary: A Video-On-Demand ad for a serum made misleading claims that it was clinically proven to reduce hyperpigmentation in two weeks.
ready.action: The ad should not appear again in the form complained of. We told L’Oréal (UK) Ltd t/a Garnier not to state or imply that Garnier Vitamin Cg Serum was clinically proven to reduce hyperpigmentation in two weeks unless they held robust evidence to substantiate their claim.

ready.name: Pets Corner UK Ltd t/a Pet Food Expert
ready.summary: A homepage for a website providing information about pet food falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their trade by misleadingly presenting the website as independent.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Pets Corner (UK) Ltd t/a Pet Food Expert to ensure future marketing communications did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example, by presenting websites over which they had control as independent.

ready.name: Shop TJC Ltd t/a Ideal World
ready.summary: Two teleshopping presentations advertising watches made misleading claims about price, savings and availability.

ready.name: Sinointeractive Digital Marketing Co Ltd t/a trustedbuyerguide.org
ready.summary: A paid-for search ad for a vacuum review website failed to make their commercial intent clear and falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their trade by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Sinointeractive Digital Marketing Co Ltd t/a trustedbuyerguide.org to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example, by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites in paid-for ads.

ready.name: Xinyu International Trading Ltd t/a consumertestreports.org
ready.summary: A paid-for search ad for a vacuum review website failed to make their commercial intent clear and falsely implied they were acting for purposes outside their trade by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Xinyu International Trading Ltd t/a consumertestreports.org to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example by presenting websites used for marketing purposes as independent review sites in paid-for ads.

ready.name: Iceland Foods Ltd t/a Iceland and The Food Warehouse
ready.summary: A banner ad and a display ad for Iceland Foods broke the rules by featuring identifiable less healthy food products.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Iceland Foods Ltd t/a Iceland and The Food Warehouse to ensure their paid ads on the internet were not for identifiable less healthy foods.

ready.name: Lidl Northern Ireland Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram post for Lidl by influencer Emma Kearney broke the rules by featuring an identifiable less healthy food product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Lidl Northern Ireland Ltd t/a Lidl to ensure their paid ads on the internet were not for identifiable less healthy foods.

ready.name: Untamed Cat Food Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram post on Untamed Cat Food’s account misleadingly made comparative claims with identifiable competitors and made misleading claims relating to the meat content of a cat’s diet and their product or rival brands.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Untamed Cat Food Ltd to ensure that any comparative claims did not mislead and that they held evidence to support their claims. We also told them to ensure that any claims relating to the meat content of a cat’s diet and their product or rival brands, did not mislead.

ready.name: Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for an online pharmacy was socially irresponsible and likely to cause harm or serious and widespread offence by exploiting new mothers’ insecurities about body image and perpetuating pressure for them to conform to body image stereotypes.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper to ensure their future advertising was prepared with a sense of responsibility to consumers and society and did not include gender stereotypes that were likely to cause harm or serious or widespread offence. We also told them not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper
ready.summary: Posts in weight-loss support groups on Facebook didn't make clear they were paid for by the advertiser and they promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, which is against the law and our rules.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper to ensure that their future posts were obviously identifiable as marketing communications and made clear their commercial intent, for example by including clear and prominent identifiers, such as “#ad”. We also told them not to promote POMs to the public in future.

ready.name: Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper
ready.summary: Two paid-for Instagram ads for an online pharmacy promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, which is against the law and our rules. They also created an undue sense of urgency for members of the public who are considering medicated weight-loss programmes.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Juniper Technologies UK Ltd t/a Juniper not to promote POMs to the public in future and to ensure their future advertising did not create an undue sense of urgency for consumers considering medicated weight-loss programmes.

ready.name: Persons unknown t/a Cloud Nine
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad for a clothing company made medical claims for a product that didn’t have the relevant compliance labels and wasn’t registered with the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Persons unknown t/a Cloud Nine not to make medical claims for a product that did not have the applicable conformity marking and was not registered with the MHRA. We also told them not to make claims that discouraged the essential treatment for a condition for which medical supervision should be sought.

ready.name: 222 Collective Group Ltd t/a 222collectiveuk
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook and Instagram ad for a food supplement brand made claims that their supplements could prevent, treat or cure the symptoms of the menopause and Pre-Menstrual Syndrome (PMS).
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the forms investigated. We told 222 Collective UK t/a 222collectiveuk not to state or imply their food supplements could prevent, treat or cure human disease, which for the purposes of the Code included claims to treat or cure the symptoms of the menopause and PMS.

ready.name: DrinkWell Beverages Ltd t/a Drinkwell
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for an online alcohol retailer misleadingly implied a drink may be preferred due to its alcohol content and made non-permitted health and nutrition claims about alcoholic drinks.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told DrinkWell Beverages Ltd not to imply that a drink may be preferred because of its alcohol content and not to make health or non-permitted nutrition claims about alcoholic drinks.

ready.name: Gallaher Ltd t/a JTI UK
ready.summary: A paid-for in-app ad promoting awareness of illegal tobacco misleadingly claimed that half of shops in the given area sold illegal tobacco, without having adequate evidence to back up this claim.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Gallaher Ltd t/a JTI UK to ensure their future ads did not claim that half of shops in a given area sold illegal tobacco unless they held adequate substantiation.

ready.name: Kaocommerce Ltd t/a Lunera
ready.summary: Two paid-for Meta ads for a food supplement brand made claims that their supplements could prevent, treat or cure symptoms of the menopause and inflammation. The ad also made unauthorised health claims.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the forms investigated. We told Kaocommerce Ltd t/a Lunera not to state or imply their food supplements could prevent, treat or cure human disease, which for the purposes of the Code included claims to treat or cure the symptoms of menopause and inflammation.

ready.name: Persons unknown t/a Charmfay Shop
ready.summary: A paid-for YouTube ad for a clothing company made misleading claims regarding a product including images and the materials used to make them.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Persons(s) unknown t/a Charmfay Shop to ensure their future ads did not include misleading claims or images regarding their products and the materials used to make them. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Polybiotics Ltd t/a Polybiotics
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook and Instagram ad and a website for a food supplement brand misleading implied their food supplements could prevent, cure or treat Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS).
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the forms investigated. We told Polybiotics Ltd t/a Polybiotics not to state or imply their food supplements could prevent, treat or cure human disease, including PCOS and to ensure that specific health claims were authorised on the GB NHC register.

ready.name: UAB CommerceCore t/a WiggyDog
ready.summary: A paid-for Meta ad for a robot-dog toy misleadingly represented and exaggerated the functionality and appearance of the product through claims and images that it behaved and looked like a real dog.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told UAB CommerceCore t/a WiggyDog to ensure their ads did not misleadingly represent or exaggerate the functionality and appearance of their products in future, for example, by stating or implying through claims or images that their product looked or behaved like a real dog.

ready.name: Centre of CPD Excellence
ready.summary: A website for an accreditation company made misleading claims it had panels of specialists, independent industry experts, accreditation against internationally recognised standards and official relationships with insurance partners.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told the Centre of CPD Excellence to ensure that future comparative claims, including price comparisons, made with identifiable competitors were not misleading, were supported by documentary evidence and could be verified by the audience.

ready.name: Grind Coffee Roasters Ltd t/a Grind
ready.summary: An ad on Grind’s own website for its coffee pods failed to make the basis of a price comparison clear and misrepresented their competitor product’s end-of-life arrangements.
ready.action: The ad should not appear again in the form complained of. We told Grind Coffee Roasters Ltd t/a Grind to ensure that their future price comparisons were not misleading by failing to make the basis of the price comparison clear.

ready.name: Humantra UK Operations Ltd t/a Humantra

ready.name: Health Bridge Ltd t/a Zava

ready.name: MedExpress Enterprises Ltd t/a MedExpress
ready.summary: Three Instagram posts and a TikTok video for weight-loss injections promoted prescription-only medicines to the public, against the law and our rules.

ready.name: Menwell Ltd t/a Voy

ready.name: UK Meds Direct Ltd

ready.name: ZING Oral Care Ltd t/a ZING Toothpaste

ready.name: Co-operative Group t/a Co-op

ready.name: Kind Patches Ltd

ready.name: Kit & Kin Ltd

ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form assessed. ready.name: The Cheeky Panda Ltd

ready.name: Mamedica Ltd

ready.name: TUI UK Ltd

We told Byrokko to ensure their ads did not irresponsibly or misleadingly claim or imply that using their product during sunbed use could help consumers achieve a tan quickly and safely. ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form investigated. We told JD Tanning UK Ltd t/a Tan & Deliver Home Hire Sunbeds to ensure they did not discourage essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought, including psoriasis.

ready.name: SFJ Group Ltd t/a SunShine Co

ready.name: Tanbox Towcester Ltd

The ad also discouraged essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought, including seasonal affective disorder (SAD).
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Tanbox Towcester Ltd to ensure they did not discourage essential treatment for conditions for which medical supervision should be sought, including seasonal affective disorder (SAD).

ready.name: The Sun Company (Horsham) Ltd t/a The Sun Company
ready.summary: A paid-for Instagram ad for a tanning studio was socially irresponsible and misleading by suggesting that tanning could be obtained safely.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form investigated. We told The Sun Company (Horsham) Ltd t/a The Sun Company to ensure that their ads were socially responsible and did not mislead consumers by suggesting that tanning can be obtained safely.

ready.name: Whiskey & Wealth Club Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for Facebook ad, landing page and website for a whiskey cask investment company made misleading claims about investment returns. The ad also failed to make clear that cask whiskey investments were unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Whiskey & Wealth Club Ltd to ensure that their future ads did not quote average or maximum return figures unless they held adequate evidence to substantiate those claims and they made clear returns were affected by the period of time the investment was held.

ready.name: Adamans Group Ltd

ready.summary: Two paid-for Google search ads for an art investment company failed to make clear that art investment was unregulated and that the value of investments was variable.
