ready.name: Tonic Weight Loss Surgery Ltd
ready.summary: A post on the company’s Instagram page irresponsibly trivialised the decision to have weight-loss surgery by creating a sense of undue urgency.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Tonic Weight Loss Surgery Ltd to ensure that future ads were prepared with a sense of responsibility by not creating an undue sense of urgency for consumers considering weight loss surgery.

ready.name: UK Flooring Direct Ltd
ready.summary: An ad on the company’s website misleadingly implied a particular savings offer was time-sensitive.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told UK Flooring Direct Ltd to ensure that future savings claims did not mislead and to ensure they substantiated savings against the usual selling prices of their products. We also told them not to portray promotional offers as being time limited if that was not the case.

ready.name: BetterCo Ltd
ready.summary: Three paid-for ads on Google search falsely implied that the marketer was acting for purposes outside its business and did not make their commercial intent clear.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told BetterCo Ltd t/a BetterVits & Clinical Reviews to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example by presenting websites over which they had control, as independent review websites, including in paid-for search ads.

ready.name: Ella Kate Reeves
ready.summary: Two Facebook pages for Ella Reeves misleadingly claimed she was accredited to the British Association of Counselling and Psychotherapy.
ready.action: The claim must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Ella Reeves not to claim in future that she was BACP accredited if that was not the case.

ready.name: Gamer Advantage LLC
ready.summary: An ad aired during a livestream on Twitch made misleading claims that blue-light glasses could improve sleep quality.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Gamer Advantage LLC not to make claims that their blue-light glasses could improve sleep quality in the absence of adequate substantiation.

ready.name: HeyNutrition Ltd
ready.summary: Three paid-for ads on Google search falsely implied that the marketer was acting for purposes outside its business and did not make their commercial intent clear.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told HeyNutrition Ltd t/a Trustworthy Reviews to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example by presenting websites over which they had control as independent review websites, including in paid-for search ads.

ready.name: Purolabs Nutrition Ltd t/a Purolabs
ready.summary: Two paid-for ads on Google search falsely implied that the marketer was acting for purposes outside its business and did not make their commercial intent clear.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Purolabs Nutrition Ltd t/a Purolabs & Wellness Explorer to ensure their ads made their commercial intent clear and did not falsely claim or imply they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example by presenting websites over which they had control as independent review websites, including in paid-for search ads.

ready.name: AA Ltd
ready.summary: A poster and website ad contained inaccurate claims that AA was the UK’s ‘largest provider’ for breakdown services, which could not be verified.
ready.action: The claims must not appear again in their current forms. We told AA Ltd to ensure that they held adequate evidence to support comparative claims; that the basis of any comparison was presented clearly; and that ads provided sufficient information to enable consumers to verify comparisons with identifiable competitors or signposted consumers to such information.

ready.name: London Planters
ready.summary: An ad on the company’s website misleadingly implied a product was of their own design, rather than designed by a third party.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told London Planters to ensure that future marketing materials did not mislead about who manufactured products they sold.

ready.name: SmokePops LDN
ready.summary: Three ads on Facebook and the company’s website for flavoured additives for cigarettes irresponsibly promoted smoking and contained misleading, irresponsible health claims.
ready.action: The ads should not appear again in the forms complained of. We told Smokepops LDN to ensure that their advertising did not encourage smoking or suggest that the products were safe or healthy.

ready.name: Weybury Hildreth Ltd t/a Purflo
ready.summary: A website ad misleadingly claimed that a baby bed was certified for safe sleeping, and claimed that the product met specific British Safety Standards which were not fully applicable for the product.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Weybury Hildreth Ltd t/a Purflo, to ensure that their advertising did not imply that their products had achieved specific certification when such a certificate did not exist, or had not been fully met.

ready.name: Lidl Great Britain Ltd
ready.summary: A leaflet by a supermarket made misleading claims about the prices at which various products were generally sold (recommended retail prices).
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Lidl Great Britain Ltd to ensure that that future references to RRPs reflected the price at which the products concerned were generally sold. We also told them to ensure that they held adequate evidence to substantiate their savings claims.

ready.name: Prettylittlething.com Ltd t/a Prettylittlething.com
ready.summary: An Instagram story on Molly-Mae Hague’s account did not make clear and upfront the commercial intent behind it and was not obviously identifiable as an ad.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Prettylittlething.com Ltd and Molly-Mae Hague to ensure that their future ads were obviously identifiable as marketing communications and the commercial intent was made clear, and that identifiers such as “#ad” were clearly and prominently displayed.

ready.name: Secret Surgery Ltd
ready.summary: Ads on Instagram and Facebook promoted a prescription-only medicine and irresponsibly put pressure on consumers to have Botox procedures.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Secret Surgery Ltd not to promote prescription-only medicines to the general public in future and to ensure that their advertising is responsible. We referred the matter to CAP’s Compliance team.

ready.name: Fox Milton & Co Ltd t/a Unique Funeral Plans
ready.summary: Ads on the website homepage, Facebook and Twitter accounts for Unique Funeral Plans misleadingly implied a relationship with Sterling Trust Corporation that did not exist.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Fox Milton & Co Ltd t/a Unique Funeral Plans to ensure future ads were not misleading.

ready.name: Kane & Ross Clinics Ltd
ready.summary: An ad on Kane & Ross Clinics’ website misleadingly implied osteopathy for babies could treat constipation and infections.

ready.name: Served Drinks Ltd t/a Served
ready.summary: Three ads on Facebook and Instagram were banned for making health and nutrition claims about an alcoholic product, and for implying alcohol can overcome boredom.

ready.name: Relx (UK) Ltd
ready.summary: An Instagram story on Louis Shaw’s account was not obviously identifiable as an ad and promoted unlicensed, nicotine-containing e-cigarettes on social media.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of.

ready.name: Wild Drinks Group Ltd t/a Whisp Drinks
ready.summary: We banned an ad on Rosie Breen’s TikTok page for making health claims about an alcoholic product, encouraging excessive drinking and featuring someone under 25 years of age.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Wild Drinks Group Ltd t/a Whisp Drinks and Rosie Breen not to make non-permitted low calorie nutrition claims about alcoholic drinks, and to ensure that future marketing communications for alcoholic drinks did not encourage excessive drinking or show people who were, or appeared to be, under 25 years of age in a significant role.

ready.name: OPTILASE (UK) LIMITED
ready.summary: An online promotion for laser eye surgery was found to be misleading and irresponsible.
ready.action: The promotion must not be run again in its current form. We told OPTILASE (UK) LTD t/a Optilase Clinic to ensure that future promotions did not mislead by omitting significant terms and conditions or material information. We also told them to ensure that future promotions were prepared with a sense of responsibility to consumers and to society.

ready.name: Person(s) unknown t/a Good Health Today
ready.summary: We banned an online ad for a company claiming to be able to treat depression and other medical conditions, over unsubstantiated claims over treatments’ efficacy.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the forms complained of. We told Person(s) unknown t/a Good Health Today and Urhealth-Matters not to claim or imply, including by the use of testimonials, that their treatment could treat health conditions, unless they held robust scientific evidence to demonstrate that was the case.

ready.name: Capri Sun GmbH
ready.summary: A banner ad was unlikely to be obviously identifiable as such by its audience, young children, and therefore ‘enhanced’ disclosure was required.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Capri Sun GmbH to ensure that ads were obviously identifiable to their audience, and used ‘enhanced’ disclosure where required.

ready.name: First Trenitalia West Coast Rail Ltd t/a Avanti West Coast
ready.summary: A website for a train company made misleading claims that its ticket prices could not be beaten.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told First Trenitalia West Coast Rail Ltd t/a Avanti West Coast to ensure that their advertising did not claim, or imply, that their ticket prices could not be beaten, without adequate qualification. We also told them to ensure the terms of any price promise were sufficiently clear.

ready.name: IMC Toys UK Ltd
ready.summary: A banner ad was unlikely to be obviously identifiable as such by its audience, young children, and therefore ‘enhanced’ disclosure was required.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told IMC Toys to ensure that ads were obviously identifiable to their audience, and used ‘enhanced’ disclosure where required.

ready.name: IMC Toys UK Ltd
ready.summary: A banner ad was unlikely to be obviously identifiable as such by its audience, young children, and therefore ‘enhanced’ disclosure was required.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told IMC Toys to ensure that ads were obviously identifiable to their audience, and used ‘enhanced’ disclosure where required.

ready.name: Take Stock Foods Ltd
ready.summary: A paid-for TikTok post for a soup company broke the rules by claiming that its food products could treat or cure acne.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Take Stock Foods Ltd not to state or imply that their food products could prevent, treat or cure human disease.

ready.summary: An Instagram post promoting a prize draw did not award prizes as described and was not administered fairly.

ready.name: Trailfinders Ltd
ready.summary: A holiday brochure was misleading because it did not make it sufficiently clear that special offers on free nights and free room upgrades were subject to restrictions.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Trailfinders Ltd to ensure that ads made it sufficiently clear if offers were subject to restrictions and included significant information about the restrictions.

ready.name: U K Insurance Ltd t/a Churchill
ready.summary: A banner ad was unlikely to be obviously identifiable as such by its audience - young children, and therefore ‘enhanced’ disclosure was required.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told U K Insurance Ltd t/a Churchill to ensure that ads were obviously identifiable to their audience, and used ‘enhanced’ disclosure where required.

ready.name: Evergreens (UK) Ltd t/a ArtificialGrass.com
ready.summary: A website and two YouTube video ads for artificial grass were misleading as they overstated the environmental benefits and air purifying qualities of the products.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Evergreens (UK) Ltd to ensure their advertising did not overstate the environmental benefits and air purifying qualities of their products.

ready.name: Partex Global GmbH
ready.summary: A website for auto parts omitted material information about the advertiser’s geographical location and misleadingly implied that the advertiser was based in the UK, when that was not the case.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Partex Global GmbH t/a Autodoc/Buycarparts.co.uk to ensure their advertising did not misleadingly imply that they were based in the UK and to make sufficiently clear the geographical address from which they operated.

ready.name: Sky UK Ltd
ready.summary: A TV and a poster ad for Sky Mobile was likely to mislead because Sky UK Ltd did not provide objective comparative evidence to substantiate its claim that it was the perfect network.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained about. We told Sky UK Ltd t/a Sky Mobile not to make claims that Sky Mobile was the perfect network unless they held objective comparative evidence to substantiate the claim as it would be understood by consumers.

ready.name: Tesco Stores Ltd t/a Tesco
ready.summary: A cross-media ad (TV, radio, Twitter, press, VOD, website) by Tesco made misleading claims that Plant Chef products could make a positive environmental difference to the planet compared to their meat equivalents.

ready.name: Verisure Services (UK) Ltd t/a Verisure
ready.summary: Claims on a website by a provider of security alarms that it offered the best alarm technology on the market were misleading and were not verifiable.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Verisure Services (UK) Ltd to ensure that they had adequate substantiation to support claims, including comparisons with identifiable competitors, in their marketing materials. We also told them to ensure that, in future, consumers were able to verify comparisons against identifiable competitors made in their advertising.

ready.name: Bier Nuts Ltd t/a Bier Company
ready.summary: An email and a text message for a mail order beer subscription service misled consumers by falsely claiming or implying they had won a prize of “free beer for life”.

ready.name: Magnatech Technology Ltd
ready.summary: A website for a company providing magnet technology for boiler systems made misleading claims the product would improve fuel efficiency, thereby saving energy and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Magnatech Technology Ltd to ensure that their future ads did not claim that their products could improve fuel efficiency, save energy or reduce greenhouse gas emissions, without adequate substantiation.

ready.name: Stacey Bradley
ready.summary: Two local press ads, one print and one digital, misleadingly implied they had been placed, endorsed or approved by a public body and misleadingly implied COVID-19 vaccinations were unsafe and illegal. They were socially irresponsible and caused fear without justifiable reason.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Stacey Bradley that their future ads must not misleadingly imply they had been placed, endorsed, or approved by a public body, including by unauthorised use of their logos.

ready.name: Stephen Bear t/a Pink Panther Models
ready.summary: A website for an adult webcam modelling recruitment agency made misleading earnings claims and inaccurate statement about the organisation’s experience in the sector.

ready.name: CheaperWaste Ltd
ready.summary: A website that included a page for comparing waste companies did not make clear it was for the purposes of lead generation, misleadingly presented the nature of the services office and implied that they were price comparison services when that was not the case.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Marketing Position Ltd and Cheaperwaste to ensure they did not misleadingly imply that they were acting for purposes outside their trade, for example by presenting websites designed to generate leads for other companies as independent comparison websites.

ready.name: Liquid Lipo Ltd
ready.summary: A product listing on a website that claimed a gel could assist with the reduction of body fat was misleading as the advertiser did not provide robust clinical evidence to prove its efficacy.
ready.action: The ad must not appear again in its current form. We told Liquid Lipo Ltd to ensure that they did not state or imply that their product could reduce body fat unless they held robust clinical evidence to substantiate their claims.

ready.name: Brand Evangelists for Beauty Ltd

ready.action: The ad must not appear again in the form complained of. We told Brand Evangelists for Beauty Ltd not to state or imply that their product could promote hair growth, help reduce thinning and lead to thicker hair unless they held adequate evidence to support their claims.

ready.name: Lucy Isabella Beauty & Aesthetics t/a Lucy Isabella
ready.summary: We banned an ad for advertising Kenalog, a prescription-only medicine, to the public.

ready.summary: We banned an ad for a private investigation agency for having unsubstantiated claims.

ready.name: Sarean Aesthetics

ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Sarean Aesthetics not to promote prescription-only medicines to the general public in future.

ready.name: Skincodes Aesthetics
ready.summary: We banned ads for marketing prescription-only medicine to the public.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told Skincodes Aesthetics not to promote prescription-only medicines to the general public in future.

ready.name: The Skin Clinic Faversham t/a The Skin Clinic
ready.summary: We banned ads for marketing prescription-only medicine to the public.
ready.action: The ads must not appear again in their current form. We told The Skin Clinic Faversham not to promote prescription-only medicines to the general public in future.

ready.name: Leisure Wear Ltd t/a SnuggyUK

ready.name: My Pharmacy (UK) Ltd
ready.summary: We upheld complaints about ads for a vitamin supplement .

ready.name: Oneade

ready.name: Skill on Net Ltd
ready.summary: We banned ads for a gambling product for being misleading and irresponsible.

ready.name: Virgin Media Ltd

ready.name: Mondelez UK Ltd
ready.summary: A website ad for a Cadburys promotion was banned for omitting significant terms and conditions.
ready.action: The promotion must not be run again in its current form. We told Mondelez UK Ltd t/a Cadbury to ensure that future promotions did not mislead by omitting significant terms and conditions or material information.

ready.name: AppQuantum Publishing Ltd
ready.summary: We upheld a complaint against an ad for a mobile game that showed inaccurate gameplay footage.

ready.name: Stillbloom Ltd

ready.name: The England and Wales Cricket Board Ltd

ready.name: Lidl Great Britain Ltd t/a Lidl UK GmbH, Lidl

ready.name: Sighthound Welfare UK Ltd t/a C.A.G.E.D
ready.summary: A billboard ad for a greyhound welfare pressure group was banned for being misleading.

register_row: Breathe Services Ltd (BSL), a debt advice company based in Bolton, first came to the attention of the ICO as part of a wider investigation into complaints received about unsolicited phone calls to potentially vulnerable individuals. In a failed attempt to hide their real identity, BSL was found to have spoofed its outbound phone number by presenting over 1,000 different telephone numbers on calls. In March 2023 the ICO carried out a search at BSL’s office in Bolton, seizing evidence including documents and electronic devices. Our extensive investigation revealed that between March - July 2022 and October - December 2022, BSL bombarded people with 4,376,037 unsolicited direct marketing calls to numbers that had been registered to the Telephone Preference Service (TPS). This resulted in 58 complaints to the TPS and a further 193 complaints to the ICO.
